title: Graduated traffic partitioning and evaluation slate for graduated fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and runway a graduated traffic-partitioning plan for deploying a new fallback strategy that routes requests to progressively cheaper model variants as load increases or latency anomalies occur. This ticket codifies milestone checkpoints, the eval slate, gating thresholds, instrumentation requirements, and cross-team responsibilities so the rollout is measurable and automatable. The plan must allow automated escalation to stronger models and safe rollbacks.

Scope: orchestration of traffic splits, evaluation criteria (quality and safety), SLO checkers, sample-size calculations, dashboards, and alerting for each phase. Does NOT include low-level kernel optimizations or quantization changes; those are tracked in ENG epics referenced in dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A documented, signed-off milestone plan with thresholds for promotion and rollback. 2) Measurement plan and dashboards instrumented in observability with token-level cost and latency breakdowns. 3) Automated gating that can pause or shrink traffic for a given variant based on predefined metrics. 4) Evaluation artifacts (prompt sets, human review rubric, A/B test config) uploaded to the eval repository. 5) Dry-run simulated traffic test executed and postcheck report validated by reliability and product leads.
milestones: M1: Milestone doc and metric contracts signed (2026-02-18)
M2: Instrumentation and dashboards live in staging (2026-02-25)
M3: Eval slate finalized and human-review rubric completed (2026-03-03)
M4: Canary: 1% traffic partition for 48h with automated gating (2026-03-07)
M5: Graduated expansion to 10% then 50% based on gates (2026-03-14)
M6: Full rollout and postmortem playbook (2026-03-15)
measurement_plan: Primary metrics: median p50 latency, p95 latency, per-token cost, prompt-level quality score (automatic classifier + sampled human labels), safety-exception rate, regen-rate (user retries), and success-rate for downstream tooling. Statistical tests: sequential A/B with pre-specified alpha=0.01 for quality regressions and Bayesian stopping rules for latency. Minimum sample sizes: 10k prompt-level observations per variant for classifier-based metrics and 1k human-labeled prompts for each major vertical. Rollback gates: any >10% relative regression in quality metric (95% CI), p95 latency increase >25% absolute, or safety exceptions >0.01% absolute change. All thresholds are preliminary and require cross-functional signoff.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-flagged staging validation (no external traffic). Phase 1: 1% canary for 48 hours with automated gating. Phase 2: 10% for 72 hours if no gates tripped. Phase 3: 50% for 7 days with per-hour checks. Phase 4: 100% gradual ramp over 48 hours if all gates clear. Fallback behavior: immediate traffic shrinking to previous stable variant + alert to on-call; automated rollback if human-review triggers confirm quality drop. All phases run with increased sampling for human review and synthetic A/B test traffic to stress specific prompts. Monday 09:00 UTC deployments only for visibility.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Small but critical quality regressions not captured by automatic metrics. Mitigation: increase human sampling and priority-review queue for high-impact prompts.
Risk: Latency spikes due to autoscaler cold starts. Mitigation: reserve warm capacity for canaries and coordinate with Dedicated team to pin nodes during rollout.
Risk: Dashboards missing token-level breakdowns. Mitigation: ENG-4120 to finish trace plumbing before M2.
Risk: Conflicting experiments running in same traffic domain. Mitigation: consult experiment scheduler and lock traffic namespace for rollout window.
Risk: Insufficient statistical power for niche verticals. Mitigation: segment gating and extended sampling windows for low-volume customers.
Risk: Security/compliance impacts from routing PII to different deployments. Mitigation: verify routing constraints with Security team; ensure KMS policies if necessary.
Risk: Automated rollback churn due to noisy metric. Mitigation: add hysteresis and require sustained threshold breach for 2 consecutive checks before automatic rollback.
